L6.1.quote: Since $x\in S$, it has gcd greater than 1 with each of $a_1,\ldots,a_n$. The minimality in the definition of $a_{n+1}$ therefore gives $a_{n+1}\le x$. Hence $x=a_{n+1}$.
L6.1.note: Characterization of terms as the increasing enumeration of admissible integers >= a_1 is proved correctly.

L6.2.note: No large-prime erasure. Finiteness rests on a false 'finite blocker' lemma; pairwise intersecting families can have infinitely many minimal transversals.

L6.3.quote: Membership in $S$ depends only on the residue class modulo $L$, because each $b_j$ divides $L$. Let $T$ be the number of residue classes modulo $L$ which belong to $S$.
L6.3.note: Assembly from n=1 written correctly but conditional on the unproved (false) finiteness of minimal transversals.

parsed.notes: Characterization and the periodicity assembly are cleanly written, but the whole finiteness step is a false set-theoretic lemma (pairwise-intersecting families can have infinitely many minimal finite transversals). No arithmetic large-prime erasure appears, so L is never shown to exist.
